To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a model of word segmentation that learns word meanings produces segmentations that are more similar to adult segmentations than a model that ignores meaning; and (2) the model that learns meaning produces more adult-like segmentions for the meaning-bearing (i.e., non-function) words.

(i) a Bayesian model for word segmentation that incorporates word meanings proposes more word-like segmentations than a model without word meanings and (ii) the model that learns word meaning proposes more adult-like word segmentations than a non-adaptive model.
(a) the model that learns word meaning segments words more accurately and (b) this segmentation accuracy is correlated with the accuracy of the word meanings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of word learning in infants, with a particular focus on the interaction between word segmentation and word learning.
the development of language and the acquisition of meaning.
the problem of how to segment speech into words.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
learning word segmentation and learning word meanings are interdependent.

the model that learns word segmentations and meanings from child-directed speech performs as well or better than the model that ignores meanings, and better than the model which ignores segmentations, on the task of segmenting child-directed speech.
word learning and segmentation are not independent processes and that the two interact with one another in a mutually beneficial way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
learning word meanings and word segmentations interact.
the word meanings are learned in parallel with word segmentation, and that word segmentation and word learning interact.
the nonlinguistic context provides important information for learning both word segmentations as wells as word meanings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
word segmentation and word learning should not be considered as two separate problems.
the two abilities may interact, but the details of the interaction are still to be discovered.
word segmentation and word learning may be more tightly coupled than is commonly believed.
